subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Which single public metadata field name and cross-channel scope should OpenClaw accept for channel group config entries, and should agent `config.patch`/`config.apply` be allowed to write it?
rationale: This changes the public configuration contract and the model-to-operator config mutation boundary, so automation should not pick the permanent field name or write policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt `name` consistently
options.body: Use one optional `name?: string` field across relevant group-entry schemas, types, generated metadata, docs, tests, and allowed low-risk config writes where intended.

options.title: Choose another canonical field
options.body: Use a different single field such as `label` or `description`, but apply it consistently and avoid aliases unless maintainers explicitly accept the larger config surface.

options.title: Decline config metadata
options.body: Keep group entries behavior-only and leave readability to docs, external notes, channel directory data, or runtime-provided display names.

recommendation.title: Adopt `name` consistently
recommendation.body: Use one optional `name?: string` field across relevant group-entry schemas, types, generated metadata, docs, tests, and allowed low-risk config writes where intended.

likelyOwner.reason: The central schema, config-contract history, and previous review evidence point to steipete as the clearest owner for the public config-shape decision.
